colors.name: ink-night
colors.role: ground — the deep night sky every drop falls from; all contrast figures are measured against it

colors.name: ink-panel
colors.role: raised panel — the verse stage floor, card grounds, the pinned section's darkening; one step above night

colors.name: petal-white
colors.role: primary text — a near-white warmed with the faintest blush; the petal at full bloom (17.2:1 on ink-night, AAA)

colors.name: bloom
colors.role: soft bloom pink — display sub-voice, the verse Korean body, the freshly opened petal (12.6:1)

colors.name: blossom
colors.role: the accent — the live petal mid-bloom: kickers, verse numerals, focus rings, ::selection ground, the card frame. Even clears AA for body text (7.8:1)

colors.name: blossom-deep
colors.role: banked blossom — functional accent on ink-panel where it must hold weight (4.6:1); the petal's shadowed edge

colors.name: gold
colors.role: the single warm mote — gold dust: the hero hairline rule, the seal stamp fill, the one drifting pollen grain. Decorative but text-safe (8.6:1)

colors.name: ink-soft
colors.role: captions, the English subtitle, the colophon — the voice spoken from further into the night (7.3:1)

colors.name: moss-ink
colors.role: large or decorative only — far petals, hairline rules, the waterline shimmer. 3.1:1, never body text

fonts.role: every Japanese glyph — the vertical 桜花 title (tategaki), verse markers 一二三, seals; a mincho drawn for vertical metrics first. The decorative source voice of the sakura motif
Korean main voice — 벚꽃, the verse body, ledes, footer; the brush-remembering Korean serif that actually speaks. 한국어 메인
Latin subtitle — the SAKURA wordmark, English subtitle, captions, numerals; a quiet noble serif, the register of a slow letter

texture: Night in three static layers (the sky is old, not alive): (1) one fixed full-viewport SVG feTurbulence pass — fractalNoise baseFrequency 0.62, 2 octaves, seed 7, stitchTiles — mapped by feColorMatrix to blossom at ≤4% alpha and screened over everything (a fine grain like dust suspended in night air, never animated); (2) a deep radial vignette, transparent at center fading to rgba(0,0,0,0.55) at the corners, holding the eye toward the waterline; (3) the waterline itself — a single 1px hairline of moss-ink at 38% opacity with a 2px blossom glow beneath it, the only fixed geometry on the page. The petals carry no texture: they are flat filled paths, the way a woodblock print is flat.

motion.name: ease-bloom
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) — every entrance: opens fast, settles long, like a petal unfurling

motion.name: ease-ink
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1) — the drop's fall and the seal press: deliberate, weighted, symmetric

motion.name: curl-field
motion.value: ψ = valueNoise(170px lattice) + 0.4·valueNoise(64px, ×1.3 anisotropy); v = (∂ψ/∂y, −∂ψ/∂x), ε = 2.5px, gain 720 — divergence-free, so petals drift and coil but never compress

motion.name: field-drift
motion.value: 14 px/s — the noise field itself drifts leftward and upward, so gusts travel with the petals instead of petals swimming through frozen wind

motion.name: ink-fall
motion.value: drop accelerates at 580 px/s² from rest, terminal 480 px/s; on striking the waterline (y = 0.42·H) it splashes (4–7 micro-droplets, life 0.5s) and spawns a bloom of 8–14 petals

motion.name: petal-drift
motion.value: buoyancy −22 px/s (petals sink gently, like real blossoms on still air) · velocity relaxation 1.8 s⁻¹ · life 7–13 s · size 7–16px growing 1.4× then fading

motion.name: bloom-burst
motion.value: on splash, petals spawn in a ring of radius 6–18px with outward velocity 40–90 px/s, angular spread ±0.8 rad from radial; rotation 0.6–2.4 rad/s, each petal a 5-pointed notched path

motion.name: pointer-wind
motion.value: horizontal pull ≤ ±70 px/s toward the cursor, gated by energy attack 0.06 / release 0.02 per 60fps frame — petals lean toward a hand fast, forget it slowly

motion.name: scroll-bloom
motion.value: pinned verse section: scroll progress 0→1 across ~2.5 viewports drives (a) ink-drops spawned at a rate of progress·1.4/s, (b) a petal-density floor of progress·0.7, (c) the current verse crossfade — petals accumulate as you read, clear as you leave

motion.name: ambient-breeze
motion.value: 18·sin(0.19t) + 9·sin(0.43t + 1.4) px/s — two periods (~33s, ~15s) with no common divisor, so the idle garden never loops

motion.name: glyph-cadence
motion.value: 1100ms ease-bloom per glyph; title 95ms/letter, verse lines 70ms/glyph with 540ms/line — the unhurried pace of petals, not a UI tick

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: 900ms ease-bloom, translateY(16px) → 0, 80ms stagger per observer batch

motion.name: ambient
motion.value: waterline shimmer 6.2s · hint drift 8.6s — mutually prime, opacity/transform only
